programme.desc: When DCI Barnaby and DS Troy arrive in the sleepy village of Badger's Drift to investigate the sudden death of elderly Miss Emily Simpson, her next door neighbour insists that she had been murdered, after she had seen her return from a walk in the woods, unnerved and shocked by something she had witnessed. programme.title: Midsomer Murders

programme.title: Midsomer Murders

programme.desc: A disused airfield near Morton Fendle is the location for a romantic evening between young Simon Bright and his girlfriend Laura Sharp - absolutely nothing could ruin their date. The next morning, when Frances Kirby is out for her morning jog, she notices the vintage car they were in up at the airfield, containing Simon Bright's dead body, with Laura nowhere to be seen. Confused, Detective Chief Inspector Barnaby and D.S. Jones can't work out whether it was a suicide pact or murder. Furthermore, they've got to find Miss Sharp and their investigation leads them to linking Simon and Laura with the villagers of Morton Fendle, who met at Elaine Trim's dancing classes. Eventually, the Barnaby family plus Jones make it to a 40s style dance night at the village hall before more villagers start turning up dead.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: When Faith Alexander arrives in Midsomer County to meet her long-lost uncle Rex Masters, she gets a shock - Rex's staff had been told that she was dead. Things become even more complex when Rex's body is found in a nearby river, bearing wounds that suggest he was murdered. Barnaby and Jones are soon on the case, trying to establish who would have wanted the elderly man dead. Several people soon come forward with multiple wills, which confuse the matter, but when two more people, close friends of Rex, are also murdered, the investigation raises question on the motive, leading Barnaby to wonder if it was down to finances, passion, or something from Rex's past.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: Following the death of Alan King while on a business trip to China, the family company, King's Crystal, is in financial trouble. As plans to shut the Midsomer Magna factory are being put into action, Alan's wife Hilary and brother Charles are married in the village church - much to the dismay of Alan's son Ian. In addition to strife between members of the family, the factory workers are outraged at the loss of their jobs. So when company accountant Peter Baxter is found murdered, Barnaby and Jones suspect a disgruntled employee is to blame. But in order to investigate the matter further, Jones is forced to work undercover, and infiltrate the local group of Freemasons in the village.

programme.title: Midsomer Murders
programme.desc: The music lovers of Midsomer County are delighted when a host of bands arrives for the Midsomer Rocks festival. Barnaby himself is particularly looking forward to seeing recently re-formed rock band, Hired Gun, perform on stage, but he soon gets close to the band for rather unfortunate reasons. During their opening performance, the band's singer, Mimi (Suzi Quatro), falls to the ground dead - electrocuted by a wire that had been run through the microphone stand. Barnaby and Jones soon find the rest of the band could be targets, and when another is killed, questions are raised as to whether former band member, Ginger Foxton, who went missing for 30 years and is presumed dead, is still at large. The detectives soon have to delve into a world of rock music, drug use and greed, to find the truth.

Once on the ground, the team confirms their setups and puts Winchester’s Supreme Long Range ammunition to the test as they glass expansive hillsides, pick apart coastal terrain, and carefully plan each move. From quick opportunities along the shoreline to calculated stalks in the high country, every moment demands focus and precision. Against the backdrop of Alaska’s wild beauty, this episode highlights the challenge, the strategy, and the performance it takes to capitalize when the opportunity finally comes together.

programme.title: Storytellers
programme.desc: We’re kicking off a special weekend at Legends Ranch in Bitely, Michigan — bringing together two groups connected by a shared respect for the outdoors. Legends Ranch has always stood forstrong conservation values, and when you combine that with the work being done by the SCI Foundation and Sables, it sets the tone for something bigger than just a hunt. Sables members are deeply involved in shaping the future of hunting — reaching intoclassrooms, working with young people, collaborating with wildlife professionals, and engaging leaders at both the state and national level. Their efforts are centered on helping others understand wildlife diversity, the principles behind the North American Model of Wildlife Conservation, and the role hunting plays in maintainingbalance in the wild. They’re also helping keep the tradition alive — showing that hunting still has a strong place in today’s culture and communities. With that kind of purpose behind it, this weekend is about more than time in the field — it’s about continuing something that matters.

programme.title: Dr. Romantic Ep.12 (English Dub)
programme.desc: An advanced death certificate needs to be signed by Dong Joo. He refuses to do so, but President Do and Hyeon Cheol urge him to act quickly against his will. Dr. Kim comes into the office just in time to witness the act. A cardiac arrest happens in the emergency ward, which prompts Dong Joo and Seo Jung to team up against the call of death. Another day in Doldam is another day of broken and mended hearts.

programme.desc: In Bum reveals the condition of Chairman Shin to Dr. Kim. His heart condition doesn't seem great, and he wants to assist in the operation. What appears to be a mere urge to take action is unknowingly a plot assembled by the president to keep an eye on Dr. Kim during his alleged unethical practice. An eager Seo Jung catches up on her mentor and gathers information to solve the medical case.

programme.title: Dr. Romantic Ep.14 (English Dub)
programme.desc: Dong Joo succumbs to the fatigue, and he ends up contracting the MERS virus. Although Dr. Kim wants to take over, Seo Jung stops him from risking his life for it. programme.title: LEGO Marvel Super Heroes: Avengers Reassembled
programme.desc: The Avengers must now fight one of their own, and they're not sure what to do! Cap and Thor lead the charge, but can't fend off Iron Man and Ultron's Minions. Meanwhile, Black Widow, Hawkeye and Hulk track down a signal that seems to be controlling Iron Man from a castle in the “Little Sokovia” section of New York. There they fight HYDRA and BARON VON STRUCKER and learn that YELLOWJACKET is the “bug” that infected Iron Man's suit for Ultron. To help break Iron Man free from Ultron's control, the Avengers call in their own bug...ANT MAN! The Avengers prepare for a party with a surprise guest when Ultron crashes the preparations by using mind control on Iron Man. While trying to rescue their leader, the rest of the team discovers that Baron Stucker, HYDRA, and Yellowjacket are in on Ultron's plans. While preparing for a party at Avengers' Tower, THE AVENGERS (IRON MAN, CAPTAIN AMERICA, BLACK WIDOW, HAWKEYE, THOR, HULK and VISION) notice Iron Man acting strangely. When Iron Man volunteers to go out and get more ice, they find it odd: when has Tony every volunteered to get anything? Suddenly, ULTRON appears on a screen: he's taken control of Iron Man! To make matters worse, Ultron takes over all the versions of Iron Man's armor and they fly off! Finally, the Avengers confront Ultron and his Ultron Minions as they attack Avengers' Tower. Ultron's ultimate plan: use all the data/stuff they've stolen to free the newly rebuilt IRON LEGION, destroy the Avengers, and control the world. Tony dons the hastily repaired Hulk Buster Armor and it's on! It's a huge battle as the Avengers try to save their beloved HQ and defeat Ultron. Will they succeed? And, more importantly, can their party be saved after Ultron tries to take down their Tower?

programme.title: The Book Of Obsession
programme.desc: The Knights are tasked with protecting the King's valuable Ned Knights comic book during the Bookingheim Knight-a-Con. But with all the costumed kids there, will they recognize the real Jestro and Book of Monsters coming to get them? King Halbert instructs the Knights that they must take his valuable Ned Knights comic book to the “Knight-a-Kon” in Bookingham. It will be the first be first prize at the Knight-a-Kon. But the Book of Monsters wants the book, too. Having devoured Ned Knightly comic books in it's down time it has become fanatically obsessed with the storyline. General Magmar suggests they simply attack the place and take what they want, but Jestro tells them they can't: everyone will be in costume and they'll be thousands of comics there. This calls for a clever “infiltration” mission (which will also allow Jestro to see the Kon, which he's always wanted to do.) So Jestro goes into the Kon with the BOM and some monsters. And it's easy because everyone is in costume Jestro, the BOM and their monsters fit right in at the convention and Clay and crew have their work cut out for them trying to separate fiend from fan. Macy keeps going on-and-on about the story in the King's comic book as the Knights keep a watchful eye on it. Robin even shows up in the “Minitrex” – a small version of the Fortrex he built just for the Knight-a-Kon. He's convinced he can win the costume competition that is the big closing event for the Kon. At the end of the Kon there's a big awards ceremony for “Best Costume.” The prize: “Ned Knightly, Knight of Knighton, Issue #1.” The BOM must get it and scheme to get closer to it during the costume contest. He's just…about…to get the book when…the impatient Magmar attacks! Everyone thinks it's part of the big show! “Ned Knightly, Knight of Knighton, Issue #1” is tossed from person-to-person-to-person in the melee. The Knights must do something, but they're too far away from the Fortrex to download any NEXO-Power. Robin pulls up in his Minitrex they can use it to get NEXO-Power! Robin wins the best costume for his Minitrex and wins the Ned Knightly Comic which he then gives to Macy…she deserves to read it.

programme.desc: When it comes to fishing and the marine industry, we are often more united by the Bluefin tuna than we think. For Ali Hussainy, the Bluefin is responsible for fueling his life long passion as an angler, and in this episode he gets to share that passion with two friends that have their own ties to the species. For wildlife biologist Forrest Galante and master sushi chef Hiroyuki Terada, catching a bluefin tuna on rod and reel will be a first!

programme.title: Local Knowledge
programme.desc: The Local Knowledge crew heads to Catalina Island off the coast of Southern California to participate in the 2024 War Heroes On Water tournament. This event offers a unique opportunity for the sport fishing community to create meaningful connections with our nation's heroes while raising awareness of the challenges they sometimes face when transitioning back to civilian life. With a little bit of luck and a lot of teamwork, Ali and Rush hope to put their veterans on a Bluefin tuna bite they won't forget!

programme.title: Winchester Life
programme.desc: In this episode of Winchester Life, a special goose hunt in South Dakota becomes a memorable day in the field as Foster heads out with Shadow, his 14-year-old black Lab and longtime hunting partner. With the season bringing challenging conditions and Shadow slowing down with age, the goal is simple: enjoy the hunt and give Shadow one more opportunity to do what he loves. As the geese begin to move, the hunt delivers an unforgettable series of retrieves and a chance to reflect on the countless hunts and memories the two have shared over the years. From Shadow's early days as a hunting dog to becoming a beloved part of the family, his impact reaches far beyond the field. With each retrieve, the day becomes less about the harvest and more about celebrating a hunting partner who has given 14 years of loyalty, determination, and unforgettable memories. As Foster looks toward future hunts without Shadow by his side, one thing remains certain—the memories they made in the field will never be forgotten.

programme.title: Garden Rescue

programme.title: Garden Rescue

programme.title: Garden Rescue

programme.title: Gardeners' World

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: It is the autumn equinox and Monty celebrates the season's apple bounty. Monty also plans for Christmas when he plants bulbs to brighten dark winter days, and he gives advice on planting garlic for the following year.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: Monty has tips and ideas for planting up garden pots to provide a focal point over the winter months, Rachel visits the tulips of Keukenhof, Joe visits Esther Rantzen's much-loved garden, and Carol visits Glebe Cottage.

programme.title: Big Dreams, Small Spaces
programme.desc: One couple battle to turn a clay-clogged building site in Sussex into a piece of Portugal. Another tackle a forest of overgrowth in their new back garden in Cadeby. They are determined to create a productive space, something they have always wanted.

programme.title: Big Dreams, Small Spaces
programme.desc: A truck driver from Wakefield with a passion for flowers wants to create a perfect outside space for his girlfriend and burgeoning family, while in Swindon a widow wants to find the best way of turning her bleak patch of green into a cottage garden.

programme.title: Big Dreams, Small Spaces

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As Monty brings in the summer harvest, he gives advice on what to sow to keep the crops coming up to the end of Autumn. Carol Klein visits a woman who is losing her eyesight and gives her recommendations of plants that will be a feast for her senses.

programme.title: Gardeners' World
programme.desc: As autumn gathers momentum, it's time to start putting the garden to bed for winter. Monty Don has some timely advice on what to do. Carol Klein meets a nurseryman in Herefordshire, and together they indulge in the beauty of the Japanese maple.

programme.title: Big Dreams, Small Spaces
programme.desc: Monty helps two families create dream gardens that are as much for the children as for the adults. In Doncaster, Nikki and John want a garden full of edible plants and fruit.

programme.title: Exploring the Mayan World
programme.desc: Traveling to Izamal, the "yellow city" named after the Maya sky god; touring the city's history, including a walk through the Convent of St. Anthony of Padua; venturing to Chichen Itza; looking at the achievements of Maya architecture.

programme.title: Exploring the Mayan World
programme.desc: A trip to Valladolid and Ek' Balam, two places in the Yucatan; the first offers travelers a chance to see a traditional agave distillery and an all-female troop of competitive horseback riders; the second is the ruins of what was once a Maya capital.

programme.title: Exploring the Mayan World
programme.desc: Accompanying Dr. Barnhart as he writes his name in Maya hieroglyphs; talking to howler monkeys; plunging into a geological cathedral; a journey to Tihosuco, home to an episode of an oppressed people fighting for their independence.

programme.title: Exploring the Mayan World
programme.desc: Exploring the history and culture of Mayapan and its surrounding region; the destruction of sacred Maya codices during public acts of faith held by the Spanish friar Diego de Landa; sampling dishes of grilled pork and ground pumpkin seeds.

programme.title: Exploring the Mayan World
programme.desc: Discovering what makes Uxmal a marvel of Maya urban planning; Dr. Barnhart explores archeological features, including the Pyramid of the Dwarf, the Palace of the Governors and the Nunnery Quadrangle; exploring the Loltun Caves.

programme.title: Exploring the Mayan World
programme.desc: Looking at Kabah, where one will find over 200 faces of Chaac the rain god and a rare example of literate public art; visiting Becal, famous for producing some of the best jipijapas in the Yucatán; taking a trip to the Celestun biosphere.

programme.title: Exploring the Mayan World
programme.desc: Labna is an architectural wonder crowned by three buildings, which are the Palacio, the El Mirador pyramid and the Labna Arch; decoding the cultural messages in these famous works; traveling back to Merida.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.desc: Learning about the Dead Sea Scrolls and their discovery; ancient Judaism and early Christianity prior to the scrolls; the uncovering of the scrolls and how they alter one's understanding of every aspect of the historical period of their creation.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.desc: Diving into a tale of excitement and adventure and discovering more about how scholars gain access to the first seven scrolls discovered at Qumran; what they find when they begin to translate the extraordinary initial discoveries.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.sub-title: Opening and Reading the First Scroll
programme.desc: Immersing into the text of the scrolls, starting with the scroll known as the Community Rule or Manual of Discipline; the important text that gives one the first insight into the community and theology of the scrolls' creators and guardians.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.sub-title: The Historical Backdrop of Ancient Judaism
programme.desc: Examining history prior to the scrolls, beginning with the biblical period and moving to the Maccabean revolt; the arrival of the Romans; King Herod's reign; the life of Jesus; the Zealot revolt; the destruction of Jerusalem and the fall of Masada.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.sub-title: The Rise of the Jewish Sects
programme.desc: Jewish sectarianism in late antiquity; focusing on the Sadducees, Pharisees, Essenes and Zealots through Josephus, the Jewish philosopher Philo and the authors of the New Testament books; the later rabbis; Roman polymath Pliny the Elder.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.sub-title: The Dead Sea Site of the Qumran Sect
programme.desc: Visiting the isolated region of Qumran's caves; learning how archeological excavations of a nearby ruin help scholars form the most accepted hypothesis of who writes the scrolls and why the scrolls are deposited in the caves.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.sub-title: The Emergence of the Rabbinic System
programme.desc: Stepping forward in time and examining some later rabbinic texts from the third century; the rise of the rabbinical tradition; vital perspectives on the composition of the Dead Sea Scrolls.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.sub-title: A Dead Sea Scroll from Medieval Cairo
programme.desc: Two copies of the Damascus Document are discovered in a Cairo synagogue in the 1890s; although the copies are medieval, the texts are believed to be ancient, a conclusion later confirmed when fragments of the same texts are found at Qumran.

programme.title: Exploring the Mayan World
programme.desc: A trip to Mérida, the capital of the Yucatán; visiting a factory hosting the revival of an industry that made the Yucatán rich more than 100 years ago; the mansions lining Mérida's Paseo de Mont; shopping for the perfect hammock and guayabera shirt.

programme.desc: A trip to Valladolid and Ek' Balam, two places in the Yucatan; the first offers travelers a chance to see a traditional agave distillery and an all-female troop of competitive horseback riders; the second is the ruins of what was once a Maya capital.

programme.title: Exploring the Mayan World
programme.desc: Accompanying Dr. Barnhart as he writes his name in Maya hieroglyphs; talking to howler monkeys; plunging into a geological cathedral; a journey to Tihosuco, home to an episode of an oppressed people fighting for their independence.

programme.title: Exploring the Mayan World
programme.desc: Exploring the history and culture of Mayapan and its surrounding region; the destruction of sacred Maya codices during public acts of faith held by the Spanish friar Diego de Landa; sampling dishes of grilled pork and ground pumpkin seeds.

programme.title: Exploring the Mayan World
programme.desc: Discovering what makes Uxmal a marvel of Maya urban planning; Dr. Barnhart explores archeological features, including the Pyramid of the Dwarf, the Palace of the Governors and the Nunnery Quadrangle; exploring the Loltun Caves.

programme.title: Exploring the Mayan World
programme.desc: Looking at Kabah, where one will find over 200 faces of Chaac the rain god and a rare example of literate public art; visiting Becal, famous for producing some of the best jipijapas in the Yucatán; taking a trip to the Celestun biosphere.

programme.title: Exploring the Mayan World
programme.desc: Labna is an architectural wonder crowned by three buildings, which are the Palacio, the El Mirador pyramid and the Labna Arch; decoding the cultural messages in these famous works; traveling back to Merida.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.desc: Learning about the Dead Sea Scrolls and their discovery; ancient Judaism and early Christianity prior to the scrolls; the uncovering of the scrolls and how they alter one's understanding of every aspect of the historical period of their creation.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.desc: Diving into a tale of excitement and adventure and discovering more about how scholars gain access to the first seven scrolls discovered at Qumran; what they find when they begin to translate the extraordinary initial discoveries.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.sub-title: Opening and Reading the First Scroll
programme.desc: Immersing into the text of the scrolls, starting with the scroll known as the Community Rule or Manual of Discipline; the important text that gives one the first insight into the community and theology of the scrolls' creators and guardians.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.sub-title: The Historical Backdrop of Ancient Judaism
programme.desc: Examining history prior to the scrolls, beginning with the biblical period and moving to the Maccabean revolt; the arrival of the Romans; King Herod's reign; the life of Jesus; the Zealot revolt; the destruction of Jerusalem and the fall of Masada.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.sub-title: The Rise of the Jewish Sects
programme.desc: Jewish sectarianism in late antiquity; focusing on the Sadducees, Pharisees, Essenes and Zealots through Josephus, the Jewish philosopher Philo and the authors of the New Testament books; the later rabbis; Roman polymath Pliny the Elder.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.sub-title: The Dead Sea Site of the Qumran Sect
programme.desc: Visiting the isolated region of Qumran's caves; learning how archeological excavations of a nearby ruin help scholars form the most accepted hypothesis of who writes the scrolls and why the scrolls are deposited in the caves.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.sub-title: The Emergence of the Rabbinic System
programme.desc: Stepping forward in time and examining some later rabbinic texts from the third century; the rise of the rabbinical tradition; vital perspectives on the composition of the Dead Sea Scrolls.

programme.title: The Dead Sea Scrolls
programme.sub-title: A Dead Sea Scroll from Medieval Cairo
programme.desc: Two copies of the Damascus Document are discovered in a Cairo synagogue in the 1890s; although the copies are medieval, the texts are believed to be ancient, a conclusion later confirmed when fragments of the same texts are found at Qumran.

programme.title: The Middle Ages Around the World
programme.sub-title: Medieval Beginnings: The Fall of Empires
programme.desc: Turbulent events that marked the beginning of the Middle Ages.

programme.title: The Middle Ages Around the World
programme.desc: Joyce E. Salisbury provides insight into the relationship between sophisticated medieval cities and their supporters.

programme.title: The Middle Ages Around the World
programme.sub-title: The Rise of Islam and Europe's Knights
programme.desc: The expansion of Islam and how people fared under Muslim rule.

programme.title: The Middle Ages Around the World
programme.desc: The cultural transformations that Muslim rule brought to its domains.

programme.title: The Vikings
programme.desc: Hostile Christian sources demonize the Vikings; Muslim accounts render them exotic; revisionist historians belittle the Norse raids; archeological finds combined with a study of the Norse sagas enrich the understanding of Scandinavia's medieval past.

programme.title: The Vikings
programme.sub-title: Land and People of Medieval Scandinavia
programme.desc: Scandinavia's landscape shapes its culture; dense forestation leads to close-knit communities; woodworking and sailing are the key means of long-distance travel; harsh winters engender skill in cold-weather commute; the emergence of great halls.

programme.title: The Vikings
programme.sub-title: Scandinavian Society in the Bronze Age
programme.desc: The physical evidence paints a picture of the Bronze Age in Scandinavia; Viking ancestors trade Arctic goods, amber and slaves in exchange for foreign copper and tin; new wealth fosters larger villages; the beginnings of the Norse pantheon.

programme.title: The Vikings
programme.sub-title: Scandinavia in the Celtic and Roman Ages
programme.desc: Scandinavia survives on trade with the Celts; contact with Rome enriches the upper classes; Scandinavians returning from Roman military service bring back advanced weapons and armor; petty kings and the first Scandinavian sailing ships emerge.

programme.title: Cities of the Ancient World
programme.desc: Cities are integral to modern lives; why wandering ancient humans leave the forests and plains to create settlements; the fundamental question of "why" is the first step toward understanding the inhabitants and lessons from ancient cities.

programme.title: Cities of the Ancient World
programme.sub-title: Çatalhöyük - First Experiment in Urban Living
programme.desc: Imagining a city with no streets, public buildings or common spaces; the world's first city offers an intriguing window into life in the Neolithic era; exploring the remains of Çatalhöyük's family housing, murals and religious shrines.

programme.title: Cities of the Ancient World
programme.desc: The story of the walls of Jericho in the Book of Joshua; looking past the biblical story; what architectural remains suggest about Jericho, whose ritual spaces help create a community and whose walls help define the urban environment.

programme.title: Cities of the Ancient World
programme.desc: Looking at one of the most marvelous cities in the ancient world; Uruk exhibits many of the hallmarks of ancient civilization; division of labor among its craftsmen; a class hierarchy that includes professional priests; records of art and literature.

programme.title: Late Antiquity: Crisis and Transformation
programme.desc: Exploring the origin of the term late antiquity; why this historical view better reflects the period from the third to the eighth centuries than the traditional view that Rome has a decline and fall; the major themes and issues of the course.

programme.title: Late Antiquity: Crisis and Transformation
programme.desc: The crisis of the third century, when Rome finds its frontiers threatened on several fronts; armies make and unmake emperors with alarming regularity; the literature of the period also reveals unmistakable feelings of despair and uncertainty.

programme.title: Late Antiquity: Crisis and Transformation
programme.desc: No one predicts that Rome is about to raise two of its greatest rulers, Diocletian and Constantine; Diocletian institutes a series of reforms that divide the empire into east and west; launching the last and fiercest persecution of Christians.

programme.title: Late Antiquity: Crisis and Transformation
programme.desc: Turning to Constantine; how he extends Diocletian's reforms; among them, he gives the empire a new capital at Byzantium, which he renames Constantinople after himself; he also takes the surprising step of legalizing Christianity.

programme.title: Conquest of the Americas
programme.desc: Neither the Eurocentric term 'discovery' nor the blandly neutral 'encounters' do justice to the impact of Europeans, Africans and Native Americans coming together in the New World; a collision whose causes and effects are outlined in this lecture.

programme.title: Conquest of the Americas
programme.desc: Most of the inhabitants of the Americas arrive in migratory waves from Asia between 40,000 and 2,000 B.C.; their civilizations are based on sophisticated irrigation and farming; complex religions and social structures; rivaling those of Europe.

programme.title: Conquest of the Americas
programme.desc: The Aztecs and Incas create empires built upon religions of conquest; powered by the control of water, around Lake Texcoco in Mexico and high in the Andes Mountains, respectively; the Maya develops an advanced knowledge of astronomy and mathematics.

programme.title: Conquest of the Americas
programme.desc: Europe and Africa are connected for centuries by Old World trading networks centered around the Mediterranean; in the 15th century, Spain and Portugal shift the trade out of the Mediterranean and into the Atlantic, along the west coast of Africa.

programme.title: America After the Cold War: The First 30 Years
programme.desc: The end of the Cold War is a key point in history; the rapid collapse of the Soviet Union; the fall of the Berlin Wall; delving into the American story in the early 1990s; conflicts in Kuwait and Bosnia test America's new role in a post-Soviet world.

programme.title: America After the Cold War: The First 30 Years
programme.desc: Bill Clinton's presidency dominates the domestic news in the 1990s. From his dramatic showdown with Newt Gingrich and the Republican Congress's Contract with America, this is a presidency of high drama; surveying the tumultuous decade.

programme.title: America After the Cold War: The First 30 Years
programme.sub-title: A New Millennium, George W. Bush, and 9/11
programme.desc: The end of the Cold War may have reshaped the world order, but 9/11 and the subsequent war on terror changes America; tracing the events leading up to the terrorist attack on American soil on Sept. 11, 2001; learning why 19 hijackers attack America.

programme.title: America After the Cold War: The First 30 Years
programme.sub-title: The US Wars in Afghanistan and Iraq
programme.desc: Historians discuss and debate the wars in Afghanistan and Iraq; the war in Afghanistan has some justification, given the role of Al-Qaeda in 9/11; Professor Allitt reviews the facts surrounding the war in Iraq; the war's effect on the United States.

programme.title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment
programme.sub-title: An Overview of Democracy in America
programme.desc: The course begins with a brief overview of Tocqueville's masterwork; written to educate the French about democracy; it is originally published as two separate volumes, released five years apart.

programme.title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment
programme.desc: William R. Cook introduces the young French nobleman, trained as a lawyer; his most famous book is only one achievement in a life marked by several; service as France's foreign minister; a history of the French Revolution regarded as a classic.

programme.title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment
programme.desc: Tocqueville rarely describes specific events or conversations; his letters and journals allow one to follow him on his trip; getting an excellent feel for the experiences he and his colleague, Gustave de Beaumont, have in America.

programme.title: Tocqueville and the American Experiment
programme.desc: This lecture considers the meaning and implications of what Tocqueville introduces in the first paragraph of "Democracy in America"; the foundation of the democratic enterprise; the concept he calls equality of conditions.

programme.title: America in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era
programme.desc: The key historical forces that characterize the Gilded Age and the Progressive Era; the competing ideals that define these eras; the US in 1865; the extraordinary social, political and economic changes unleashed by the devastation of the Civil War.

programme.title: America in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era
programme.desc: The Reconstruction era following the Civil War; governmental policies and legislation enacted to safeguard the welfare of former slaves and average citizens; these policies are progressively dismantled, the South comes under the rule of the whites.

programme.title: America in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era
programme.sub-title: Buffalo Bill Cody and the Myth of the West
programme.desc: The story of the conquest of the American West; key myths surrounding the West and how it is settled; the motives and realities of westward migration; the components of the western economy; the conflicts with Native Americans that lead to violence.

programme.title: America in the Gilded Age and Progressive Era
programme.desc: America rises from a developing nation status in 1865 to become a great industrial power by 1900; the unfolding of the American industrial revolution; the advent of big business in the railroad, steel and oil industries; consumerism and advertising.
